pi.name: Mesfin Mekonnen, Ph.D.
pi.title: Assistant Professor, Civil, Construction & Environmental Engineering
pi.bio: Dr. Mekonnen leads the Water Security Lab at the University of Alabama. His research focuses on interactions between human water use and natural hydrologic systems, with emphasis on water security, water footprints, drought and low-flow vulnerability, groundwater-surface-water interactions, and water-energy-food systems. His work integrates hydrologic modeling, remote sensing, geospatial analysis, and large-scale data analysis to understand water availability, use, and sustainability.

students.name: Habtamu Tamiru
students.focus: His research integrates hydrologic modeling, data assimilation, and machine learning to improve streamflow prediction and water-resource assessment.

students.name: Swatantra Kumar Sharma
students.focus: His research integrates remote sensing, hydrologic modeling, crop modeling, and machine learning to improve the estimation of evapotranspiration, soil moisture, irrigation water use, and agricultural water productivity. He develops scalable computational workflows using satellite observations and environmental datasets to support sustainable water resources management under climate variability and land-use change. Prior to joining The University of Alabama, he worked as a Project Research Assistant at IIT Bombay, contributing to watershed modeling and climate change impact assessments.

students.focus: Research focus: Leveraging big data and machine learning to advance large-scale hydrological and water availability modeling.
